page: Amazon Web Services g7.metal is a bare-metal accelerated computing server designed for graphics-intensive and GPU-bound tasks. The instance features 192 dedicated physical x86_64 cores driven by Intel processors operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz with single-thread core execution. It is provisioned with 768 GB of system memory, providing a uniform allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

Hardware acceleration is supplied by eight NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 GPUs based on the Blackwell architecture, providing an aggregate video memory pool of 256 GB VRAM. For high-speed local dataset caching and scratch space, the bare-metal host integrates 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. High-throughput data ingestion and distributed communication are supported by a 700 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

The bare-metal architecture grants direct access to physical resources without hypervisor overhead, maximizing execution efficiency for intensive graphics rendering, multi-stream video processing, and enterprise workstation hosting. With 192 dedicated physical cores and eight discrete GPUs backed by local NVMe storage and high network throughput, the host minimizes bottlenecks across parallel media pipelines, computer-aided engineering, and distributed inference workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services g7.metal is a bare-metal accelerated computing instance engineered for graphics-intensive and parallel processing workloads. The host features 192 dedicated Intel x86_64 cores operating at 3.9 GHz with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio, paired with 768 GB of system memory. GPU acceleration is delivered through eight NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 GPUs from the Blackwell architecture family, offering an aggregate 256 GB of dedicated VRAM. High-bandwidth local I/O is backed by 7600 GB of NVMe SSD storage alongside a 700 Gbps baseline network interface. Because this bare-metal host eliminates virtualization overhead, hardware efficiency is sustained across resource-dense workflows. This configuration is aligned with demanding applications including 3D graphics rendering, computer vision, distributed model inference, video encoding pipelines, and high-density virtual workstation deployments requiring substantial parallel compute and local storage throughput.
